articles.title: ‘It’s such a joy to ride:’ this cargo e-bike makes errands and commuting a breeze
articles.summary: This pricey ebike is a gamechanger for going around town, getting groceries and hauling cargo with ease – without paying for gas. The best bike lights and bike locks in the US. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Parking a car in an urban area can be stressful. Spaces are often hard to find, traffic congestion is a pain and it just takes extra time.

An electric bike changes that paradigm – you can roll up on the curb, lock your bike, and walk to your destination. Recently, I tested the Lectric XPedition2, an electric cargo bike that not only made grocery shopping easier but helped me explore my city stress-free.

Like the competing Aventon Abound and Specialized Haul, the XPedition2 is an electric bike meant to haul cargo. But this one only comes as a long-tail, meaning it has an extended rack on the back for transporting library books, groceries and even little kids.

The Lectric XPedition2 costs $1,399 which is admittedly much more expensive than an entry-level non-electric bike. Yet, it’s such a joy to ride, so stable and balanced, and lasts so long on a charge that I’ve started driving far less, especially in a downtown area. My daily errands such as coffee runs and shopping are less stressful and more enjoyable.
points: This pricey ebike is a gamechanger for going around town, getting groceries and hauling cargo with ease – without paying for gas.

articles.title: ‘12 weeks and SO disgusted by my dog’: what happens when you’re pregnant and can’t stand your pet?
articles.summary: There may be almost no research on pet aversion during and post-pregnancy, but it may not be particularly rare. About three weeks into her first pregnancy, Sylvia Luu began to loathe the smell of her border collie mix, Ranger.
body: Luu could hardly be in the same room as Ranger without becoming nauseous. His drool repulsed her, and she found the smell of his fur so disgusting she wore a nose plug all day.
“Before pregnancy, I used to smell my dog’s paws a lot,” says Luu. “But during pregnancy, I would throw up if I ever tried that.”
At the time, Luu, 35, and Ranger had enjoyed 12 happy years together. Ranger slept in Luu’s bed. She walked him in all weather, and let him lick her face.

Luu’s doctor said that her nausea was normal and simply advised her to drink more water to avoid dehydration from vomiting, but that didn’t alleviate Luu’s distress. “I was so heartbroken that I couldn’t love my dog as much as I wanted to,” says Luu, whose husband took over pet care duties. She wondered about rehoming Ranger, and was relieved when, upon delivering her firstborn, her aversion vanished.
points: There may be almost no research on pet aversion during and post-pregnancy, but it may not be particularly rare.

articles.title: Gen Z has very strong opinions about age gap relationships – and it could be right | Zoe Williams
articles.summary: Older men and younger women were once an unremarkable screen pairing. But watching them with a new generation is a real education. I looked up the cast before I saw the new film adaptation of Sense and Sensibility, thinking: “Who could be as good as Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet?” because of…
body: The notable casting update was Col Brandon, whose passion for Marianne would now be known as an “age gap” relationship. In the last film, Alan Rickman (born 1946) was in love with Winslet (born 1975), who cycles through a fair amount of: “Yuck, no thanks,” before having an epiphany.
Sorry if that spoiled the end. I don’t really see Jane Austen as a suspense-monger.

Winslet could easily have been Rickman’s daughter and, biologically speaking, just about his granddaughter. In the 90s, though, the age gap was a distant second consideration to the fact that Brandon was grumpy and boring, although his gruff exterior masked a serious mind and a heart of gold. I have my own thoughts on this romantic trope as a long‑term cohabitation prospect, but we can do those another day. Besides, look at that age gap. The term might not be all that long.

To the modern audience, however, the age gap simply wouldn’t “sit right”, as one gossip zine put it. I’m not wild about this terminology: “sit right”, “uncomfortable”. The subtext is: “You are in breach of absolutely fundamental and self-evident values, which I am too gracious and polite to mention, yet not to do so is bringing me discomfort.”
points: Older men and younger women were once an unremarkable screen pairing.
But watching them with a new generation is a real education.

articles.title: Sanjana Modha’s quick and easy recipe for baked beans butter masala | Quick and easy
articles.summary: Transform two tins of baked beans into this creamy curry. Masala baked beans, tadka baked beans, curried baked beans, spicy baked beans; all avatars of spice-laced baked beans are a mainstay of British Asian kitchens.
body: This creamy, dreamy baked bean curry is delicious with naan or served as any of the suggestions mentioned above. To make this vegan, use your favourite plant-based butter and an oat- or soya-based cream. Coconut milk also works in place of cream.

Melt the butter in a medium saucepan, then add the onion and saute for three to five minutes, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic, ginger and tomato puree, and cook for another minute, until aromatic.
Add all the baked beans, along with all the sauce from the cans, stir in the turmeric, chilli powder, ground cardamom, garam masala and salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.

Stir in the cream (reserve a few tablespoons to serve), cover the pan with a lid and leave the curry to come to a simmer over a low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often to stop the beans sticking to the base of the pan.

articles.title: This Hanging Dryer Finally Solved My Smelly Shoe Problem
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. I'm sticking to my marathon training schedule, nor'easter be damned. Normally, that means I'd come home with soaked shoes, prop them in front of a fan, and hope they dry out overnight.
body: This weekend I had two training runs back to back in the rain, which meant my shoes had to be ready to go again almost immediately. This week's upgrade is the gadget that made it work: this Hedgehog Hanger.

The Hedgehog Hanger is a hanging shoe and glove dryer. You can easily hang it in a closet or wardrobe (there's a stainless steel hook), plug it in, and slide your shoes onto its arms. Instead of just warming the air, it pushes airflow through the shoes. The brand says the patented turbine technology moves humidity out of the fabric, and that a pair of shoes or gloves dries in about 15 to 30 minutes.

I really like the control it gives you. The heat is adjustable, from room temperature up through a few warm settings, including lower ones meant for leather and more sensitive materials. That matters if you don't want to blast a nice pair of shoes at full heat. There are five speed settings, and it goes up to a "tornado" mode for the fastest drying when you're in a hurry.

articles.title: If Your iPhone 18 Pro Is Randomly Rebooting, There's a Fix
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Apple released a bunch of new devices this month. The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 support new health-tracking features and Siri AI, while the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max introduce the A20 chip and variable aperture for the first time…
body: As reported by 9to5Mac, some iPhone 18 Pro users are noticing that their smartphones are freezing up after a failed Face ID scan. When this happens, you won't be able to interact with your iPhone, even if the "Try Face ID Again" button appears onscreen. Instead, after a few moments, the iPhone will reboot. It's not a catastrophic issue, but it is annoying, and it's affecting a number of users, as this Reddit thread shows.

It's a similar story with the latest Apple Watches. While the Series 12 and Ultra 4 obviously don't use Face ID, users are still experiencing random reboots—emphasis on "random." Unlike the iPhone 18 Pro users, affected Apple Watch users aren't doing anything in particular when their watches reboot. They could be in the middle of a workout, chatting with Siri AI, or using the Maps app, when all of a sudden, the Apple logo appears. Some analyses showed that the Neural Engine was at fault, but Apple never confirmed the exact issue.
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max may unexpectedly restart when Face ID fails to authenticate.

articles.title: The Bride Wore an Antique Wax Flower Crown for Her Backyard Wedding in the Hudson Valley
articles.summary: Writer Aemilia Madden also wore vintage Christian Dior and Prada over her bucolic wedding weekend to artist Dylan Reitz, which took place at the groom’s family in Upstate New York under an old pear tree.
body: When Aemilia Madden and Dylan Reitz-Cruz first connected on Hinge in 2022, her profile said she was looking for someone with “good taste in snacks and hikes.” Dylan messaged, asking her what “bad taste in hikes” looked like. After chatting and discovering their shared interest in the author Michael Pollan and the podcast 99% Invisible, she stopped responding. Luckily, Dylan double-messaged her, and she met him for drinks at Izzy Rose in Clinton Hill, Brooklyn.

Though their first date was a classic bar meet-up, the second date was special. “Dylan planned a date in Greenwood Cemetery, making good on the ‘hikes and snacks’ conversation, planning a walk and picnic,” Aemilia recalls. Aemilia had gone to pre-school in Oakland, California, next to the city’s Mountain View Cemetery, and grew up taking daily walks through the cemetery. “When I told my family, they had a good feeling about him, and said he knew me shockingly well.”

articles.title: Why Does Rejection Hurt So Much? A Scientist Who Studies Misery Breaks It Down
articles.summary: In an excerpt from “The Opposite of Happiness: How Bad Feelings Make and Break Us,” Carnegie Mellon professor George Loewenstein turns his attention to one of the most devastating, and enduring, forms of misery: rejection.
body: In Plato’s Symposium, the character of Aristophanes relates a myth about how people once had a “double nature.” Instead of one face, they had two. Instead of four limbs, they had eight. Possessed of tremendous strength and agility, they could walk upright but also bend themselves into circles and roll around at high speed. Such fearsome creatures posed a threat to the gods on Mount Olympus. Should they be annihilated? Zeus chewed on the question for a long time before a eureka moment came to him.

“Methinks I have a plan which will humble their pride and improve their manners,” he said. “Men shall continue to exist, but I will cut them in two and then they will be diminished in strength and increased in numbers; this will have the advantage of making them more profitable to us.”

Zeus sliced the ur-people into two halves, and dispatched Apollo to clean up the mess. Apollo yanked skin, sculpted breasts, forged mouths. When he was finished, each person looked at their newly detached other half—and panicked. They flung their arms around each other, entwined, longing to be one again, until “they were on the point of dying from hunger and self-neglect.”

articles.title: Green Chili
articles.summary: I will happily eat a bowl of chili any time of year, but once the weather starts to cool down it’s one of the first things I want simmering on my stove. There are so many different variations of green chili — and depending on who’s making it, no two pots are exactly the same.
body: Tomatillos, poblanos, jalapeño, hatch chiles, and fresh cilantro give the chili its bright, savory flavor, while fire-roasted tomatoes, oregano, and cumin add depth. I personally love adding white beans for a little extra texture and heartiness, but they are completely optional. Serve with a generous spoonful of sour cream, diced avocado, fresh cilantro, and plenty of crunchy tortilla chips for scooping. This is the kind of cozy, satisfying dinner that only gets better as it sits, and it’s one I look forward to making as soon as chili season rolls around.

After spending a few years working with Rachel Ray, who I consider the chili queen, I learned a thing or two about building a deeply flavorful chili without making it feel overly heavy. Combined with over a decade of food media and development experience, I love bringing what I’ve learned to home-cook everywhere.
Pat 2 pounds boneless pork shoulder pieces dry with paper towels. Season with 1 teaspoon of the kosher salt and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.

articles.title: On the Podcast: How Mikey Madison Prepared for Her Role in ‘The Social Reckoning’
articles.summary: In this Monday’s special episode of “The Run-Through,” October cover star Mikey Madison joins Chloe at her hotel room in Milan to discuss playing Facebook whistleblower Frances Haugen in Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” out October 9.
body: Madison does not physically resemble Haugen—nor did Sorkin want her to—so she had to embody the character in other ways. “For this one, I feel like it’s more of an intellectual transformation that I needed to try and pull off,” she explains. “There was a lot of restraint involved in this character and how she processes emotions, and so that was something that was intriguing to me—also, a little bit scary in a way.”

Outside of work, Madison spends most of her time baking or spending time with her family and pets, which include two donkeys. “There was one point where I was like, I wonder, is this too crazy and unhinged? ” Madison says, referring to her menagerie. (She also has three Chihuahuas and a cat.) “ Like, are people gonna think that I’m crazy? And then I was like, you know what? This is me.”
